why: Commit 3 asks the executor to 'open localizePage() and check, field by field' which translated fields the grid's SQL must mirror. The brief's own expressions get it wrong: translations are flat text keys ('seo.description', 'thumbnail.alt', src/lib/page-translation.ts:308-309), not nested objects, and mapTexts also cuts each text to a length. Commits 4 and 5 lean on publishedPageIndex(), indexTitle() and PAGE_INDEX_FIELDS from steps 0.24 and 2.14, whose fields are not given. They also ask for judgement: open each rg hit and decide which statements 'can return more than one row with a whole document', and whether the blog listing's caller moves. Sitemaps and llms.txt are public output, and articleCards is a new 'use cache' read.
harm_if_wrong: Translated grid cards and feed entries would show the base language's search description or picture alt, and sitemaps or llms.txt could drop or mislabel pages. The before/after test only covers a translated title and excerpt, so it would not see either.
make_it_cheaper: Give commit 3's SQL with the flat translation keys (tr ->> 'excerpt', tr ->> 'seo.description', tr ->> 'thumbnail.alt') plus the length cuts, add a translated seo description and alt to the before/after fixture, and list the exact fields 0.24's index carries. Commits 3 and 4 would then be cheap-then-review.
brief_problems: Commit 3's expressions use tr -> 'seo' ->> 'description' and tr -> 'thumbnail' ->> 'alt'. localizePage() reads translation[key] with flat keys 'seo.description' and 'thumbnail.alt' (src/lib/page-translation.ts:308-309, 364-367), so these expressions always miss the translation.
mapTexts() cuts the excerpt to 300 and seo.description to 160 characters. The SQL does not, so the cards could differ from today's.
Commit 1 leaves articles/blogs/page.tsx as 'open it: if it uses only id and title replace, else leave'.
Commit 5 asks the executor to classify every rg hit by hand into the pageDocuments list.
